And there were only two dates here. They are either the 1st of December or the 21st of December. There is no mention of them anywhere before that. So these were dates around or on the eve of the signing of the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: Yes, I have some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have some questions for you. Witness, you told us that with regard to citations and incentives, it was within the purview of General Delic, whilst when it came to decisions on decorations, they were in the purview of President Izetbegovic; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. According to the rules and book of rules, that's how it was meant to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You added -- when looking at a document submitted by the Prosecution, I believe, you said that there was a decision for a citation to be given to the El Mudjahedin Detachment. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, this decision was within the purview of General Delic only, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why not? What was the purpose of this? Why wasn't the competence of General Delic that was involved here?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood your question. What kind of competences are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The power to decide to give a citation to the El Mudjahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I explained yesterday that this decision was the decision by President Izetbegovic, by the political circles, and this document that Sulejman Vranj brought to me, this document had been seen by the president and Sulejman Vranj said that he knew what this was about because he was the one who had brought this document, this proposal from the 3rd Corps. And on orders from the president of the Presidency, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, this was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm confused now. So that decision apparently would have been an exception to the normal procedure under which citations were granted by General Delic; that would be an exception, what you're saying right now. I hadn't understood that before. So an exception to the normal procedure for citations, not decorations?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. This was quite exceptionally a decision -- an exceptional decision, extraordinary, because these were foreign citizens, and under the Dayton Accords they were to leave there, so their fate was decided by the political or politicians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to know something else from you in the same matter. Because of the position you had in your department, which delivered citations and incentives, do you know whether a citation or an incentive was given to a foreigner, to an individual who would have taken part in fights, in fighting, to defend Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know, and I can quote examples. Karmen Konda is a woman who was killed at the beginning of the war, and she was awarded a citation for recognition or merit. I think she was from Split. I think there was another recipient, a soldier who came from Germany, that he was also given this award. He was killed in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And was it General Delic who decided to give those awards, if it was decided after the 18th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I prepared the decision. I was the author of these documents, and Delic signed the order that I prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you were the drafter, the one who drafted the documents, and General Delic is the one who took the responsibility for the documents by signing them. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not in that context. Mr. Delic was the person who signed it. He was the commander and he signed it, but the decision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry. Maybe this is a question for the Chamber. There was something else I wanted to know. Are you aware of an opportunity or occasion when General Delic signed a decision to award a citation or incentive to an Arabic member, to a foreign national coming from a country of Muslim faith, for their contribution to the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina? I'm speaking about a foreigner, a foreign country.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified yesterday, Your Honour. I said that it wasn't just one individual; there were a number of people. There were documents that were signed on the 1st and 23rd of December, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but they were dealing with single individuals, even if there were several of them; this was not to do with one unit, but with individuals; right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This concerned individuals who were members of the 3rd Corps. So let me just explain this a bit. I do not regard them as individuals, but as a unit. I see the corps behind them, because the corps is the one who proposed them. They could not address the General Staff directly for any citations or incentive, as individuals or as a unit. If -- whenever this was done, whenever proposals were made, they were made by the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you for your explanation. Do you know when the 3rd Corps made that proposal? And when it arrived, do you know whether there was any opposition or objection from General Delic? And if he did object, did President Izetbegovic intervene to overcome that problem?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Delic did not even see this proposal. It came to my office directly, to my department. And as for consultations with Mr. Izetbegovic, there were such consultations; mine, but also more of General Vranj consulted with Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who signed the decision to award the citation to these individuals who were members of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was signed by General Delic, like all the orders that were signed for all the other units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Loncaric, I, too, have two questions for you. One question relates to the purpose of giving awards to the El Mujahedin Detachment, and my other question relates to the role that General Delic had in this process. Now, as to the first question of the purpose of giving awards to the El Mujahedin Detachment and to individual members of the El Mujahedin Detachment, what I have been able to learn from your testimony here before us is that the purpose for which these awards were considered and, indeed, given to the El Mujahedin Detachment and to some of its members was to motivate them to leave the country after the signing of the Dayton Agreement. And please correct me if I'm wrong, but I think you have testified that this truly political motive for giving them these awards was the reason why no substantive arguments were advanced in support of these awards. So, in other words, what was proposed by General Mahmuljin and sanctioned by -- or approved of by the president of the Presidency, was given without any substantive support, because it didn't matter whether actually they deserved these medals; the purpose to give those medals and those awards to them was just to motivate them to leave the country. Is that correctly understood? Can I have your answer for the record?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you understood me well. And if you look at the dates, you can see -- if we are talking about December 1995, this was on the eve or after the signing of the Dayton Accords, so it's obvious that it's a political issue and that it was important to get rid of them. Had there been any other reason, then they would probably have been awarded these citations earlier on, maybe in 1994 or earlier. I think -- but this wasn't done, so I think I was clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You were indeed. But you see, the difficulty I have in understanding the implications of your testimony is that some of these documents were dated well before the signing of the Dayton Agreement. If I'm not mistaken, General Mahmuljin's proposal, the first proposal that he made which you may or may not have seen was dated 10th November, and so I would assume that the considerations about giving these awards would have started even earlier, probably in the beginning of November or maybe even by the end of October, the idea of seeking ways to give them these awards were first taken up.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer to the extent of my abilities or knowledge. Before the signing of the Dayton Accords, a month or two earlier, there was talk about the accords. The Dayton Accords were not signed in a period of two days. They were under discussion for a longer period. And as for the anniversary and the proposal, where it came from, I cannot really answer. I cannot answer relating to that part, but I can say that all this was done in the context of the Dayton Accords, before they were signed and after they were signed, because it was politically obvious that they needed to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Who told you this? Who told you that the Dayton Accord would include provisions about foreign fighters leaving the country? You were not, yourself, a member of the negotiating team, were you, so how did you learn about the relation between awards to El Mujahedin members and the contents of the Dayton Accord?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that when discussing the anniversary, that this was the motive. But as for the Dayton Accords, they were discussed in the meetings of the party, the town -- at the town board meetings, and we were informed, of course -- before the accords were signed, we were informed of the substance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me, why would receiving an award provide a motivation for a foreign fighter to leave the country?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I know that that's what Mr. Izetbegovic said to Sulejman Vranj. So all I said here was what I had heard, that it was proposed that they should be awarded these citations. This was probably proposed in a meeting. And as agreed, it was acted upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And your understanding of what General Vranj told you was that awarding them or giving them these awards would facilitate their departure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But you did not, yourself, understand if this was conducive to the goal of having them leave the country?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Vranj had good information, that he was often out in the field, and that he knew them most because he was in contact with the officers of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as with President Izetbegovic, and I believe that he did have the information and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the last word the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Loncaric, could you please repeat the last part of your answer, because it was not picked up by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vranj was an officer of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina who enjoyed most respect in the party, in general, and on the part of President Izetbegovic, who placed the most trust in him, and I believe that he had the right information and he knew what he was telling us when he was talking about the need for these people to be awarded -- to be given these awards in order to, in fact, get rid of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to move on to my second question, which is the question of the role that General Delic played in all of this. My starting point is that I'm not sure I have understood your testimony fully, because on the one hand, the rules and regulations applicable to awards would seem to involve, as a natural factor, the army commander. On the other hand, you have testified that this was really a political decision, especially in respect of the El Mujahedin unit and its members, and so all decisions regarding awards to these gentlemen were political and, thus, taken behind General Delic's back. Do you understand what I have said?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's correct. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So we are told by you that the reason why General Delic was kept out of all this was that it was truly a political matter and that he, as army chief, should not interfere with these matters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe -- or, rather, I know for sure that Rasim Delic was not a member of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That may well be, but still the first part of my assumption was the army commander, by implication of his position, would be that of course he would be involved in the awarding of units and members, and indeed he did sign some of the letters, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he signed them, but in times of war I believe a great many things change. It is one matter to be a commander in time of peace and quite another in time of war. In time of war, it is highly questionable, the issue how far your authority goes and to what extent you can issue someone with orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This is a very broad answer to my question. I would have thought it was really otherwise or the other way around, really, that in times of war the command structures are strengthened. But be that as it may, the core of this matter is that you are saying that there is a pro forma authority with the army commander, a legal authority, if you want, to sign some of the award letters, yet the substantive dealing with awards to the El Mujahedin Detachment was really a political matter that was decided upon outside the military structure?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So if this is correctly understood, then I just want to ensure that I have understood correctly that although the question of El Mujahedin awards was decided upon by a political body outside the military structure, then, on the other hand, the army commander would still formally and legally hold responsibility for these matters; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally and legally, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is 12.00. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a few questions, sir. Was President Izetbegovic a member of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And of the SDA as well?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And Mr. Rasim Delic was a member of neither?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And Sakib Mahmuljin, was he a member of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was he a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, when you were asked by Judge Harhoff, I think you said that Mr. Izetbegovic gave awards, citation awards, to units and individuals. Did you say so?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say he gave them to individuals?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I thought you had said earlier that he only gave them to units. Hadn't you said so earlier, before you were asked by Judge Harhoff?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Decorations were within the competence of the Presidency and were awarded to individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And citations?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Citations and incentives were within the competence of the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And didn't you say that Mr. Izetbegovic gave citations to member of the El Mudjahedin Detachment? I'm just checking. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He ordered that they be awarded, but it was not within his competence to award them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So they were awarded by Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising from the questions by the Bench, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, one question only, in order to clarify the last matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: His Honour asked you the following: They were given awards, citations, by General Delic? Do you recall exactly what sort of citations these were?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit received an incentive which is that of a commendation, whereas individuals were awarded commendations and a certificate of merit, which was an incentive, and these were a golden shield and:

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Another thing the interpreter didn't catch.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I believe we have the transcript a bit confused, and I think it's due to the translation, and that's because both the decoration and everything is interpreted with one word, and we are talking about different matters because we're talking about citations and decorations. That's why I put the question. Thank you, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we can clarify the last issue, which also arose during the questions from Judge Lattanzi, by simply looking at the law. I believe the law is relatively straightforward on the point, who had the competence to make awards. It was Exhibit 1375. The problem is that the translation is only a partial translation. That's why we had earlier submitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you? Do you have something that you want to clear with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please go ahead and clear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could have 6291 being shown, please. That's about the question of incentives and awards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, if you focus for a moment at paragraph 3, please, if we could enlarge because it's very difficult to read, I believe, paragraph 3 or Article 3. Yes, thank you. We see here we have Golden Lilies, number 1, Silver Shield, the Gratitude Lily, number 3, and the Plaque of the Armed Forces of the RBiH. Could you explain briefly who was competence to give these awards?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was within the competence of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you refer to "commander," which commander are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were referring, in a couple of answers to Judge Lattanzi's question, to decorations. Could you briefly explain, in contrast to these four awards we see here in Article 3, what are the decorations you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean as opposed to citations and these awards here? Well, the difference is in the fact that the decorations are awarded by the Presidency pursuant to a different book of rules adopted by the Presidency, and the difference lies also in the fact that a citation is an award of a lower level than decorations, because the decorations are awarded by the president of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand that. Could you briefly say what type of decorations the Presidency could issue?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can think of a couple of decorations, the Liberty Medal, a medal with golden swords, a medal with silver swords, and such like.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you tell briefly which office was competent to process the documents which related to decorations of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. My department processed the proposals, and we took them to President Izetbegovic. I've already explained that previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So do I understand your testimony, then, you could get a request from the Presidency, would process it, and the Presidency would then sign it, the decorations?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not the procedure applied for decorations. The decorations awarded by the president were processed in the following ways: Sulejman Vranj would go to see the president, and together they would make a list of army members who ought to receive decorations, and then they would bring the list to me. I would process the list, and then it would be taken back to the president to be signed. But this was not a large group of people who were awarded this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand. So if we look back at this law here, this law refers to Golden Lily, Silver Shield, and Gratitude Lily, and the Plaque of the RBiH. The proposals for these four types of citations, who would make the proposal?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proposals for citations and incentives were submitted to the General Staff, that's to say to my administration and department, by the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think the issue is clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not clear. I'm confused. Just one or two questions. The acknowledgments mentioned in Article 3, what are they? Are they decorations or are they something other than decorations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. What it says, that's what it is. That's a citation, a war citation; Golden Lily, Silver Shield, they were citations, whereas the medals were within the competency of the Presidency and were not regulated by these rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Article 3 refers to citations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Article 4 refers to incentives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Decorations are dealt with by another law, not this law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I guess that brings us, then, to the conclusion of your testimony, sir. Thank you so much for taking the time to come and testify at the Tribunal. We have now come to the end of your testimony. You are free to go, you are excused, and may you travel well back home. And once again, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the next witness we can call only on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. In that event, then, the matter stands adjourned to Monday, the 14th of April, at 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.
